verdicts.title: Grid peeling and the affine curve-shortening flow
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper we study an experimentally-observed connection between two seemingly unrelated processes, one from computational geometry and the other from differential geometry. The first one (which we call "grid peeling") is the convex-layer decomposition of subsets $G\subset \mathbb Z^2$ of the integer grid, previously studied for the particular case $G=\{1,\ldots,m\}^2$ by Har-Peled and Lidický (2013). The second one is the affine curve-shortening flow (ACSF), first studied by Alvarez et al.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns grid peeling and affine curve-shortening flow in computational/differential geometry, with no mention of Kähler manifolds or SAT clause subset complexity. The Θ(n^{3/2}log n) bound is about grid points removed in peeling iterations, unrelated to the conjecture's claim.
